attractions.name: Bala Hisar Mound
attractions.description: An ancient archaeological mound believed to be part of the historic Gandhara city of Pushkalavati, one of the region's oldest urban sites.

attractions.name: Shaikhan Dheri Archaeological Site
attractions.description: Excavated ruins of the ancient Gandhara-era city, revealing layers of Buddhist and Indo-Greek era history.

food_places.name: Charsadda Chappal Kebab stalls
food_places.specialty: Charsadda is famous nationwide for its large, flat chappal kebab

weather_info.climate_type: Warm plains climate, hot summers and mild winters

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and pleasant, 8-20°C, ideal for sightseeing

travel_tips.tip: Visit Charsadda in the warmer months (roughly May to September) if it's a mountain area, since roads can close in winter snow.
Shared vans (Suzuki/Hiace) and intercity coaches are the main way to reach and travel around the district.
Arrange accommodation and local transport in advance, especially in more remote mountain areas.

history.founded: Site of the ancient Gandhara city of Pushkalavati, one of the oldest continually-inhabited areas in South Asia
history.city_history: Charsadda was the ancient capital of Gandhara (Pushkalavati) and a major Buddhist-era center; archaeological mounds like Bala Hisar and Shaikhan Dheri reflect over 2,500 years of continuous settlement.
history.province_history: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (formerly North-West Frontier Province) has been a historic crossroads between South and Central Asia for millennia, home to Gandhara civilization sites, the ancient Silk Road route through the Khyber Pass, and a mix of Pashtun tribal, Mughal, Sikh, and British colonial influence before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947. In 2018, the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA) were formally merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as regular districts.
